summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of Console focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdown. Customer interested in cost optimizations and dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive inference; asked about security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Agreed to pilot benchmark and receive pricing + security docs.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 14:30 PDT - Duration 42m - Attendees: Maya Chen, Samir Patel (Redwood); Olivia Grant, Diego Ramos, Priya Singh (Nova Commerce)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll get started in a minute, i'm maya from redwood, and with me is samir on the se side.
00:08 Olivia: hey thanks, we appreciate it. we've been poking at your api docs and some of the benchmark notes. excited to see the console.
00:16 Maya: cool, quick agenda - console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and how you can see per-token costs. then q&a and next steps. sound good?
00:27 Diego: yep sounds good, our main questions are cost visibility and how to map costs to product routes, also SLOs for latency.
00:35 Samir: perfect. i'll share my screen - okay, so this is the console home. real quick note: some names in the ui are 'Readwood' in older builds - ignore that, it's just a label bug we've seen.
00:48 Samir: over on the left is analytics -> usage. here you get token counts, request counts, and group by model, route, and api key. you can also filter by time windows and export CSV.
01:05 Olivia: nice, can we see per-route cost? like cart-checkout vs search-autocomplete?
01:13 Samir: yeah that's the per-route dashboards. switching to 'per-route' - see each route has its own throughput, p50/p95 latency, token breakdown, and importantly a cost column that maps to token pricing and any batching discounts.
01:30 Priya: i like that. is the cost shown realtime or batched daily?
01:36 Samir: it's near realtime - we update estimates within a few minutes. final reconciled billing runs daily. so the console is for operational visibility, billing invoices may differ slightly.
01:48 Diego: how do you attribute multi-model fallbacks? sometimes a request starts on a cheaper quantized variant and falls back to a larger model.
01:58 Samir: good question. we attribute based on the actual served model per request. the dashboard shows 'served_model' and you can group by that. fallback events are logged and there's a column for 'fallback_reason' in the export.
02:14 Olivia: are exports structured? we want to feed this into our internal cost ETL.
02:20 Samir: yes CSV and parquet export, plus an API endpoint to pull per-route daily aggregates.
02:28 Priya: security quick - our security team will ask about SSO, audit logs, and key management. do you have SAML and KMS integration?
02:38 Maya: yes SAML/SSO for the console, RBAC roles, and for Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS and HSM workflows; hosted can integrate with cloud KMS. we'll send the security pack after this.
02:50 Diego: great. any SOC 2/ISO certs?
02:54 Maya: SOC 2 Type II in our docs, and ISO 27001 info in the pack. we'll attach those.
03:02 Olivia: perfect. back to cost - how do you represent batching optimizations? we do lots of short chats and want batching to reduce cost without hurting latency.
03:12 Samir: batching shows up in two ways: first, the runtime logs 'effective batch size' and latency distribution per batch. second, the cost model applies batching discounts at token-level so the per-token estimate decreases with larger batches; the dashboard will highlight routes with high batching benefits.
03:32 Priya: is there an automated suggestion engine? like optimize recommending quantization + batching profiles per route?
03:40 Samir: yes, that's Redwood Optimize - it suggests policies: which routes to quantize, recommended sequence length truncation, and batching window adjustments. you can preview expected cost delta and potential quality impact in the console.
03:56 Olivia: can i see an example?
04:00 Samir: sure - opening Optimize suggestions on the right. here's a 'search-autocomplete' route recommendation: switch to int8 quantization for a 2% quality drop but 40% cost savings estimated. we also recommend lowering max tokens for certain routes.
04:18 Olivia: 2% drop might be fine. does Optimize run on historical traffic or live test?
04:24 Samir: it analyzes historical traffic - we replay samples in a sandbox to estimate quality impact and cost. if you want, during a pilot we can run A/B tests against 5% of traffic.
04:36 Diego: how do you measure quality regressions? we have internal eval sets.
04:41 Samir: you can upload eval prompts or we can pull a sample; console shows per-prompt scoring differences and aggregate delta. alerts fire if regression exceeds thresholds.
04:55 Priya: about dedicated capacity - if we go dedicated can we pin model versions and have guaranteed latency SLOs?
05:03 Maya: yes, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools, model pinning, and SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. you can define autoscale policies and burst pools.
05:14 Diego: curious about routing - can requests be routed by policy, region, cost or latency?
05:20 Samir: yep smart routing supports rules: route by latency SLO, cost limit, or by region/tenant. fallback to cheaper model variants if a higher tier is saturated.
05:33 Olivia: any notes on data residency? we operate in EU and want data to stay in eu-west-1 for EU traffic.
05:40 Maya: you can set region routing policies and dedicated/private deployments in chosen region. Private on-prem options for fully air-gapped setups.
05:49 Olivia: good. can we get access to a demo instance with read-only for our data analysts?
05:55 Maya: yes, we'll spin up a read-only view for the pilot. that's part of next steps.
06:02 Samir: jumping back to the dashboard - here's token-level cost heatmap. you can filter by model type and route; it highlights routes which are cost outliers.
06:15 Diego: that heatmap is helpful, what about per-user cost attribution? we need to bill internal teams.
06:22 Samir: you can group by api key or tenant id; we support tagging routes and adding metadata to attribute cost to internal teams.
06:32 Priya: show me the alerts - what triggers can we set?
06:36 Samir: alerts on cost spike (X% over baseline), latency breaches, regression alerts on quality metrics, and custom thresholds on per-route token usage. they can send to slack, pagerduty, or webhook.
06:49 Olivia: ok, i wanted to ask about token accounting - how do you handle truncated responses or cancellation mid-stream?
06:56 Samir: we account for tokens actually generated and KB cache hits reduce token counts billed. cancelled streams bill for tokens generated until cancel. prefix caching is accounted for separately and reduces billed tokens for repeated prefixes.
07:12 Diego: do you expose KV cache hit rates?
07:16 Samir: yes, caching metrics are in the route view: prefix hit rate, cache eviction, and suggested cache TTLs based on traffic patterns.
07:27 Olivia: nice. switching to procurement questions - what's typical term for Dedicated? monthly or annual?
07:34 Maya: both; committed monthly or annual contracts with discounts for annual. we can propose a 6- or 12-month pilot with a credit applied if you convert to committed capacity.
07:46 Priya: any onboarding support? migrations?
07:50 Maya: we offer solutions engineering support during pilot and a migration playbook for large customers; dedicated customers get onboarding hours and runbooks.
07:59 Diego: can we run a pilot that includes our spotty workload - search spikes during sales events. can the system autoscale?
08:07 Samir: autoscaling is policy-driven; you can set burst capacity for sudden spikes and fallback models for cost control. for big spikes we also have pre-warm APIs.
08:20 Olivia: billing reconciliation - can we get raw usage logs for audit?
08:24 Maya: yes, raw logs with request-level metadata are available via secure S3 export or direct API.
08:31 Priya: i remember seeing a 'route-level simulated cost' in your docs - can we simulate cost for hypothetical traffic?
08:38 Samir: yes the simulator lets you upload traffic profiles or use historical traffic to model cost under different policies, quantization, and routing rules.
08:49 Olivia: do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs? some of our pipelines depend on that.
08:55 Samir: yes, the API supports structured output and function calling; the console parses structured output as well for route analytics.
09:05 Diego: what about integration with our observability stack? we use datadog and internal tracing.
09:11 Samir: we have tracing hooks and exporters for datadog, prometheus, and open telemetry. you can ingest token-level traces into your systems.
09:22 Olivia: okay, couple of nitpicks - sometimes console UI performance is slow for long time ranges?
09:28 Samir: noted - large date-range queries run async and we show a cached snapshot; there's also a scheduled daily aggregations job to speed up large queries.
09:41 Maya: quick recap before q&a closes: you'll get pricing, security pack, pilot plan, and read-only console access.
09:49 Priya: sounds good. two technical follow-ups: 1) we'll send our eval set for Optimize testing; 2) we'll provide expected QPS and route split.
09:58 Olivia: and we'll need the SOC2 report and network diagrams for the security review.
10:06 Maya: absolutely, we'll include those in the security pack.
10:10 Diego: timeline-wise, we want pilot next week if possible.
10:13 Maya: we can start setup this week; Samir will prepare the pilot plan.
10:18 Samir: i'll outline the pilot: 2-week pilot, baseline collection 3 days, A/B 10 days at 5% traffic, then compile cost/quality report.
10:30 Priya: that works. any blockers on our side?
10:33 Olivia: only approvals from procurement for pilot access, but that's internal.
10:37 Maya: great. any final q's?
10:40 Olivia: just one - do you have any references of retail customers that did a similar pilot?
10:45 Maya: yes, we ran a pilot with 'Arcadia Retail' and 'Aurora Tech' - we can share anonymized results showing 30-45% cost reductions on search routes.
10:55 Diego: thanks.
11:00 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and next steps.
11:06 Olivia: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional label mismatches and filler words. timestamps approximate to the minute; meeting lasted ~42 minutes.
